newsitem.title: USA: Grapevine, Texas officials push for new bond issue.
newsitem.headline: Grapevine, Texas officials push for new bond issue.

text.p: Grapevine, home to Dallas-Fort Worth International Airport, can afford a proposed $37 million bond issue without raising property taxes but the council may vote to keep it below $30 million, interim city manager Roger Nelson said Thursday.
Nelson said the city council will consider the $37 million bond proposal next week when it meets to discuss a $55 million budget for next fiscal year, which begins Oct 1.
But he said he did not expect the proposed package to win full approval.

"I doubt it would be $37 million. More likely it will be less than $30 million because the council may not want to go that high," Nelson told Reuters. "However, we feel we can justify $37 million without raising the tax rate. We will also be retiring some of the old bonds."
The city's property tax rate currently stands at 41.5 cents per $100 valuation.
Nelson said the proposed $37 million issue would set aside $29 million for new roads and park improvements needed to cope with the city's growth.
Other projects included in the package are a $5 million library and a $1.5 million fire station.
Situated in northeast Tarrant County, Grapevine's population has more than tripled to 35,000 since 1980.
Grapevine residents last approved a bond issue in October 1994, voting to support a $13 million issue for a new city hall, community center and street improvements.
Dallas-Fort Worth International accounts for $8 million of the city's $14 million annual property tax revenues.
